items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: So I know Gleason's talked about how he started reviewing...

ctx.x: Well, we own all that. Who was Gene Williams? And I never did quite know how he got in the picture and when and when. Was he in the book?

No, he's not. No, he was a student at Columbia University along with Ralph Gleason and a couple other people he knew like Barry Olenov is that his name, the one-time editor of Metronome and Tori Dano was another of his friends there. So I know Gleason's talked about how he started reviewing, Gleason began reviewing records for the Columbia College paper just so he could get free records, I guess, from the companies mostly. And Gene probably did some of that work too. Anyway, Gene started about as soon as he was…
Speaking about Bunk Johnson, how many people were involved really in his coming back? Was there quite a group of people interested in him? I know you played a large part.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: I looked all that up for Ralph Gleason about, uh, two or three months ago.

ctx.x: The, uh, same studio. I'd have to look that up. I looked all that up for Ralph Gleason about, uh, two or three months ago. Ralph had had the idea it was WWL. It wasn't that. Uh, that, uh, that Bunk had made his records for Jean Williams. Jean did make some records at a studio, WSMB, I guess. His—I know, WSMB, in the Maison Blanc's building in 1942. Uh, Woody, uh, I'm not real sure. I don't have the dope at hand right now. It might have been W—WL, which is the Roosevelt Hotel, possibly, at that time. But, uh,…
Well, he probably hadn't lived here since 1918, I guess.
